Anya (product): Heads-up — BigCorp legal asked for a 9-month deprecation window for the FalconX-v2 pin. They say migration requires QA + compliance signoff. Can Product team weigh in on risks? (cc @Priya @Jorge) :eyes:
Priya (sales): They signed the annual Dedicated contract; extension request is part of their procurement ask. They want indemnity language and a concrete migration timeline. They mentioned dedicated engineering support on their side.
Jorge (eng): From infra side, keeping a pinned older model for 9 months is doable but it increases runway cost and operational complexity. We'll need to keep the older weights in the hot catalog (no TTL) and maintain performance/security patches. Need a rough GPU-month estimate to share with Sales.
Samir (platform): Operational tradeoffs: dual-serving (new+old) increases KV cache size and memory pressure, and complicates autoscaling by about ~10–20% depending on traffic. We can support it if customer pays for the extra reserved capacity, or we accept an internal cost hit short-term.
Anya (product): Proposed negotiation options for Sales to present:
- Option A: Standard 6mo deprecation window (public policy) + paid 3mo extension on request.
- Option B: 9mo free extension if customer agrees to follow our migration checklist, run a 2-week canary, and accept monitoring/regression gates.
- Option C: 9mo free but with a hard cap on supported features (no guarantee on performance parity), plus surcharge for security patches.
Which seems operationally feasible?
Elena (legal): Legal prefers Option B but we must add explicit acceptance criteria and an escape clause: we retain the right to accelerate deprecation for security/vulnerability fixes. Also require customer to provide a POC and sign the migration acceptance checklist. We'll draft contract language aligning to Option B.
Priya (sales): Customer verbally prefers Option B — they want a checklist and a named Redwood contact for migration windows. They also asked for SLOs around fidelity regressions and a clause about rollbacks if quality drops.
Jorge (eng): For fidelity SLOs we can bind to metrics in our eval harness: suggest threshold triggers like embedding cosine drop > 0.02 (2%) or generation-quality delta > 5% on our standard prompt set. If triggered, we either rollback in canary or open a remediation plan. Need agreement on exact thresholds.
Samir (platform): Note: canary + rollback plan adds complexity to routing: we must support route-by-customer and per-route fallbacks. That will cost ~1-2 engineer-weeks to test and document. Also expect ~15% extra memory for KV cache while both versions are hot.
Anya (product): Action items (owner / ETA):
- Priya (sales): confirm customer acceptance of Option B and request POC + canary window (ETA: EOD Wed).
- Jorge (eng) & Samir (platform): produce cost + ops delta (GPU-months, memory, engineering effort) and proposed regression thresholds (ETA: EOD Thu).
- Elena (legal): draft contract clause and migration acceptance checklist (ETA: Mon).
- Anya (product): update internal catalog pin-exception flow and prepare PR for comms (ETA: Mon).
deploy-bot: New task created: #ticket-4821 — "BigCorp deprecation exception: contract + ops plan" (created by Anya)
Priya (sales): One more ask from BigCorp: early access to our compatibility shim / canary adapter and a 2-week Dedicated canary in their reserved pool. They want to mirror a small fraction of traffic.
Jorge (eng): 2-week canary is fine. We'll require a scheduling window and a formal rollback runbook. Quick runbook snippet for the ticket: ```canary steps:
1) mirror 5–10% traffic to canary variant
2) monitor latency, cost, and eval regressions every 6 hours
3) if any metric breaches threshold, pause canary and notify escalation list
4) if unresolved after 24h, rollback and open incident```
Anya (product): Thanks all — I'll schedule a sync with Sales + Legal tomorrow 10:00 PST to finalize the customer-facing options. Please post updates here if anything changes. Closing thread for async updates. :calendar:
